screening_decisions.reason: Compares two decision aids (long vs short) and surgeon preference report vs usual care. The intervention is decision aids, not PROMs feedback. The patient preference report is not a PROM but a summary of treatment goals. Does not directly compare PROMs feedback to no feedback.

Randomised trial. Intervention: dentists informed of patients' Modified Dental Anxiety Scale (MDAS) scores prior to treatment. Control: dentists not informed. The MDAS is a patient-reported outcome measure (PROM), and the study assesses the effect of feeding back this PROM to healthcare providers on patient anxiety. Directly compares PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

Randomised trial in a counselling service. Intervention: therapists receive session-by-session progress feedback using the ultra-brief Outcome Rating Scale (ORS), a PROM. Control: no feedback. Compares outcomes between groups. Directly addresses the effect of PROMs feedback to healthcare providers on therapy outcomes.

Compares two forms of PROMs feedback: feedback to therapist and supervisor (MeMOS) vs feedback to therapist alone (S-Sup). No true 'no feedback' control group. Does not directly compare PROMs feedback against not providing such information, but rather different feedback modalities. Excluded because the control is not absence of PROMs feedback.

Randomised trial: intervention group uses Oncokompas, a web-based eHealth application that monitors HRQOL and symptoms (PROMs) and provides tailored feedback to patients with an overview of supportive care options. Control group receives access after 6 months (no feedback during study). Directly compares PROMs feedback to patients against no such feedback. Included even though primary outcome is patient activation because feedback is PROM-based and directed to patients.
This is an integrated literature review on graphical display of PRO data. It is not a randomised trial. Study design does not meet inclusion criteria.

This is a complex mobile telehealth intervention involving self-monitoring of blood glucose, mobile-phone data transmissions, graphical and nurse-initiated feedback, and educational calls. The feedback component is not clearly focused on PROMs but on clinical measures (HbA1c, blood pressure). Though PROMs (quality of life, depression, anxiety) were measured as outcomes, the intervention is not primarily providing PROMs feedback. Multimodal intervention; not a straightforward PROMs feedback vs no feedback comparison.

Randomised trial in oncology practice. Intervention: regular completion of HRQL questionnaires (EORTC QLQ-C30, HADS) with feedback of results to physicians. Attention-control: completion without feedback. Control: no HRQL measurement. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare providers against no feedback and against measurement alone. Assesses patient well-being and communication.

Randomised trial. Intervention: physicians informed of patient's Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale scores (a PROM). Control: not informed. Assesses diagnosis and treatment of depression. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare provider vs no feedback.

Laboratory study on driving under the influence. Provides performance feedback on a simulated driving task, not patient-reported outcome measures. Not a clinical practice setting, does not involve PROMs feedback. Excluded.

Randomised trial: physicians received a screener result (anxiety symptom levels and functioning status) for patients with previously undetected anxiety. Control: physicians not informed. Uses a PROM-based screener and feeds back results to physicians. Direct comparison of PROMs feedback vs no feedback on patient outcomes.
This is a validation study of the SF-36 questionnaire as an outcome measure. It is not a randomised trial evaluating feedback of PROMs vs no feedback. Study design does not meet criteria.

Randomised controlled trial: 'Featback' intervention includes automated monitoring and feedback of eating disorder symptoms (a PROM) to patients, with varying levels of therapist support. Control: waiting list. Compares PROMs-based feedback intervention to no such intervention. Included despite cost-utility focus as it directly evaluates effects of providing PROMs feedback (automated) vs no feedback.

Randomised trial: physicians received reports summarising patient responses to a self-administered functional disability questionnaire (a PROM) every four months. Control: no report. Compares PROMs feedback to healthcare providers against no feedback on patient functional status.

Focuses on symptom perception interventions (peak flow training, resistive load discrimination) and feedback on those training tasks, not on patient-reported outcome measures. The outcomes include trigger identification and quality of life, but the feedback is about performance on physiological tests, not PROMs. Not a PROMs feedback trial.

Abstract incomplete. Describes a multimodal supportive care intervention. No clear indication of PROMs feedback vs no feedback comparison. Not sufficient evidence to include as a PROMs feedback trial.
This is a structured review of the impact of PROMs on routine practice, not a randomised trial. Study design does not meet inclusion criteria.
Abstract discusses venous thromboembolism risk in immune-mediated diseases; does not match title? Possibly wrong abstract. Regardless, not a trial of PROMs feedback.

Randomised trial: case coordinators used a pain assessment battery and depression scale; results sent to physicians and patients (experimental) vs usual assessment (control). Assesses whether systematic pain assessment information alters clinical practice. Directly compares PROMs feedback (pain, depression) to healthcare providers and patients against no such feedback.

Title suggests a feasibility study on integrating PROMs into primary care, but the abstract describes a psychometric validation of a self-care screening tool during COVID-19 lockdown. Not a randomised trial of PROMs feedback.

Randomised controlled trial: intervention group completed the Work Stress Questionnaire (WSQ, a PROM) and physicians received feedback; control group received treatment as usual. Assesses healthcare visits and treatments. Directly compares PROMs feedback to physicians against no such feedback.

Randomised trial: older cancer patients received educational materials plus monthly telephone monitoring (TM) of distress using HADS and EORTC items (PROMs) with referral if above cutoff, compared to educational materials alone. The monitoring includes feedback/referral based on PROM results. Compares PROMs-based monitoring and feedback vs no monitoring.

Multisite randomised clinical trial in psychiatric clinics: patients randomised to feedback (OQ-45.2 results provided to therapist) vs no feedback. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare provider vs no such feedback on therapy outcomes.

Pilot randomised trial: mobile app that collects symptom data (ESAS - a PROM) and provides feedback/recommendations to patients; control group usual care. Compares PROMs-based feedback and navigation to support awareness vs no such feedback. Included despite being a pilot because it is a randomised trial comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

Cross-sectional study that randomised participants to evaluate different graphic formats for presenting PRO data. Not a trial assessing the effect of PROMs feedback on health outcomes or processes of care. Excluded.

Randomised trial of preoperative knowledge feedback: intervention group received a feedback session based on a knowledge test, not a PROM. The feedback is about knowledge, not patient-reported outcomes. Excluded.
Qualitative interview study exploring GPs' opinions about severity questionnaires for depression. Not a randomised trial. Excluded.

Feasibility cluster-randomised trial of a self-management programme integrated into stroke rehabilitation. The intervention is self-management support, not specifically PROMs feedback. The self-management workbook may involve some assessment, but the core intervention is not feeding back PROMs to providers or patients compared to no feedback.

Randomised trial: patients completed a computerised psychiatric screening interview (PRIME-MD, a PROM-like diagnostic tool), and were randomised to: patient and physician told results, patient told only, or neither told. Examines effect of feeding back screening results (based on patient-reported symptoms) on psychiatric referral. Directly compares PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

This is a protocol/design paper describing the rationale and implementation challenges of a randomised trial (the Diabetes Telephone Study). It does not report outcome data. Typically, protocols without results are excluded. Does not provide evidence on effects of PROMs feedback.

Randomised trial in oncology: patients assigned to usual care, HRQL assessment alone, or HRQL assessment with structured interview and feedback of results to nurse. Compares different levels of PROMs feedback (none, assessment alone, assessment with feedback) on patient HRQL and satisfaction. Direct comparison of PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

Randomised trial: patient-reported cancer needs, QOL, and psychosocial information collected and made available to the health care team for targeted interventions vs not seen. Compares PROMs feedback to healthcare providers (with coordinated interventions) against no feedback on patient outcomes.
Protocol for a pragmatic randomised controlled trial (ZELF-i). Reports planned methods, not results. Exclude as does not provide outcome data.

The study evaluates a multi-component internet-based self-help intervention with automated feedback, not specifically the routine provision of PROMs feedback in clinical practice; it compares different levels of therapist support, not feedback versus no feedback.
This is a scoping review, not a randomized trial, and thus does not meet the study design criterion.
Randomized trial comparing two supportive care models that provided feedback of patient-reported outcomes to caseworkers or clinicians versus usual care without feedback.
Methodological article on meta-analysis heterogeneity, not a randomized trial of PROMs feedback.
Randomized trial directly comparing QoL questionnaire completion with feedback to clinicians versus no questionnaire/feedback in a clinical setting.
Randomized trial systematically varying feedback of depression screening results to physicians against no feedback in an ambulatory care setting.
Qualitative interview study exploring oncologists' views, not a randomized trial.
This is a meta-analysis and theoretical review, not a randomized trial of PROMs feedback.
Randomized trial of formal health status reports (AIMS/MHAQ) fed back to physicians versus attention placebo and control in rheumatology.
Randomized trial where pain scale summaries were provided to oncologists in the intervention group versus no summary in the control group.
Study describes the development and validation of a PRO measure assessment tool, not a randomized trial of feedback.
Trial of pharmacist-delivered tobacco cessation counseling, which does not involve providing PROMs feedback.
This is a narrative review discussing applications of PROs, not a randomized trial.
Pilot randomized trial of daily electronic PRO symptom reporting to nurses versus no reporting in an inpatient HCT setting.
Randomized trial of at-home symptom monitoring with automated alerts sent to clinicians versus no alerts, directly comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.
Randomized trial providing GHQ screening results to primary care providers for a subset of patients versus no feedback, examining detection and management.
Randomized trial comparing two active quality improvement interventions (nurse-led comorbidity programme vs patient self-assessment), lacking a no-feedback comparator arm.
Randomized trial evaluating the effectiveness of OQ-45 feedback to clinicians versus no feedback in psychiatric outpatients.
Trial compares web-mediated symptom-based follow-up (with alerts) to routine CT surveillance; the comparator is an alternative follow-up strategy, not simply absence of PROMs feedback.
This paper reports the development and psychometric evaluation of a PROM, not a randomized trial of feedback.
Pilot randomized trial of providing feedback on personality test results (patient-reported) to patients in substance use treatment versus no feedback.
This is a perspective/overview article, not a randomized trial.
Randomized crossover trial providing graphic summaries of HRQL questionnaires to both physicians and patients before consultations versus no feedback.
Randomized trial directly comparing the provision of PROMIS symptom scores to primary care clinicians versus no scores.
Randomized trial comparing QoL assessment with feedback to clinicians against QoL assessment without feedback and standard care.
Randomized trial of electronic PRO feedback to providers and families versus no feedback in children with advanced cancer.
Trial compares evidence-based screening tools to informal judgment; the focus is on screening accuracy and referral, not on the effect of providing PROMs feedback per se.
Randomized trial of a QoL diagnosis and therapy pathway that includes QoL assessment with feedback to practitioners, compared to standard care without such feedback.
This is a commentary/discussion article on a trial's results, not the primary randomized trial report itself.
Randomized trial where oncologists received or did not receive real-time electronic HRQoL data before each clinic visit.
Prospective controlled study but not clearly randomized; the allocation method is not described and likely a before-after design, so does not meet randomized trial criterion.
Includes a randomized component where depression scores were disclosed to GPs for a random subset of undetected cases, directly comparing feedback to non-disclosure.
Randomized trial of the ESRA-C tool where patient-reported SQLIs were graphically summarized and given to clinicians before visits versus no summary.

The study evaluates a flare management intervention triggered by a PROM rather than the effect of PROM feedback per se; the intervention includes nurse-led counseling and expedited visits, making it a multicomponent care pathway, not a direct comparison of PROM feedback versus no feedback.
Not a randomized trial; this is a commentary/overview of PROMs in practice.
Not a randomized trial; it is a framework/review of implementing PROs.
The study assesses a short-term life review therapy, not PROM feedback.
RCT comparing feedback of depression screening results (PROM) to patients and clinicians versus no feedback, measuring depression severity and quality of life outcomes.
The intervention is a collaborative depression care management program, not primarily a study of PROM feedback.
RCT comparing systematic screening for adverse effects using a PROM (AEP) with feedback to physicians versus usual care, measuring toxicity burden and quality of life.
RCT of a continuous feedback system (PCOMS) providing therapists with patient-reported outcome data on progress in psychotherapy, comparing feedback versus no feedback on treatment outcomes.
The intervention focuses on a mobile monitoring and feedback tool for physical activity behavior, not a patient-reported health outcome measure as defined in this review.
This is an experimental study in university students without a clinical care context, not evaluating PROM feedback in routine practice.
The study addresses screening for youth violence (a risk behavior), not the use of PROMs assessing health outcomes.
RCT of a QoL-monitor (PROM) feedback to both patients and clinicians during chemotherapy, evaluating effects on communication, satisfaction, and QoL.
RCT of providing GPs with results of a composite screening questionnaire (including PROM scales for anxiety, depression, etc.) versus no feedback, assessing recognition and care of mental disorders.
Development of a classification system for PROMs; not an intervention study.
The intervention provides alcohol screening results feedback; while patient-reported, the measures are risk behaviors, not health outcome PROMs as defined in the review.
Not an original study; appears to be a systematic review or protocol.
Intervention targets daily sun protection behavior, not PROMs for health outcomes.
The study evaluates a web-based communication tool for collaborative care, not specifically the effect of PROM feedback.
Cluster RCT directly testing the effect of providing surgeons with peer benchmarked PROMs feedback versus no feedback on patient outcomes after hip replacement.
RCT evaluating the effect of giving therapists feedback on patient progress using PROMs during psychotherapy, compared with no feedback.
RCT of providing GPs with results of a computerized PROM assessment (PROQSY) for common mental disorders versus no feedback, measuring clinical outcomes.
RCT of routine HRQOL (PROM) assessment and face-to-face discussion of results with pediatricians versus usual care, showing improved HRQOL outcomes in children with diabetes.

The STarT Back strategy uses a PROM to stratify patients into risk groups and matches treatment accordingly; the trial tests a complex stratified care intervention, not merely the effect of PROM feedback.
The study evaluates a multifaceted recovery-oriented psychiatric intervention package, not specifically PROM feedback.
This is a guidance document, not a randomized trial.
The study compares in-person counseling versus computer-generated feedback for alcohol use; it does not examine PROM feedback as defined for health outcomes.
Protocol for a trial comparing different administration modes of a PROM, not comparing PROM feedback versus no feedback.
RCT of providing physicians with SF-36 health status (PROM) results before patient encounters versus withholding, assessing impact on communication, management, and satisfaction.
Electronic screening and personalized feedback for adolescent health risk behaviors; not PROMs as health outcome measures.
A realist synthesis, not a randomized trial.

RCT of a computerized system that collects patient-reported symptoms and preferences (PROM) and provides them to clinicians before consultation, compared with no feedback, to improve symptom management congruence.
RCT of systematic screening for adverse effects using the AEP (a PROM) with feedback to clinicians versus usual care, resulting in reduced adverse effects and improved quality of life.

The intervention is a multi-component mobile health programme including self-monitoring of clinical data, educational calls, and nurse feedback. It does not focus on feedback from patient-reported outcome measures and does not directly compare PROMs feedback versus no PROMs feedback.

This randomised controlled trial directly compares providing patient progress information (based on standardised patient-reported outcome measures) to therapists, or to both therapists and patients, versus treatment as usual. It meets the inclusion criteria for a study of PROMs feedback on treatment outcomes.
This study describes the development and psychometric testing of a quality-of-life questionnaire; it is not a randomised trial and does not evaluate PROMs feedback.

This cluster-randomised controlled trial evaluates real-time electronic monitoring of patient-reported symptoms with immediate feedback (printed monitoring sheet) to oncologists versus no feedback. It directly tests the effect of PROMs feedback on quality of life and symptoms.

This group randomised trial assesses a clinical decision support system (SAMI) that provides clinicians with a longitudinal symptom report and management suggestions based on patient-reported symptoms, compared to usual care. It meets the criteria for a trial of PROMs feedback.

This randomised quality-improvement intervention evaluates real-time daily feedback of patient experience survey results to hospitalists (plus coaching) versus no feedback. Patient experience is a patient-reported measure; the trial directly compares feedback with no feedback, though it focuses on experience rather than health outcomes per se.

This study investigates the effect of providing depression screening results to physicians on medical record notation, but the abstract does not describe a randomised design. Without clear evidence of randomisation, it does not meet the inclusion criteria.
This is a Cochrane review protocol, not a primary randomised controlled trial.

This randomised trial evaluates the impact of providing physicians with detailed feedback about a patient’s mental health problem and desired interventions, with or without a counselling protocol, compared to a control group without such feedback. It fits the eligibility criteria.

This RCT assesses a technology-assisted symptom monitoring system (SM+F) that provides feedback to providers compared to usual care in prostate cancer survivors, measuring HRQoL and doctor-patient communication. It is a direct comparison of PROMs feedback.

This RCT tests computer-generated feedback to physicians about patients’ functional status (a patient-reported outcome) and chief complaint, plus educational sessions, versus no feedback. Outcome is functional status. It meets criteria.

This RCT directly compares outcome monitoring feedback (based on patient-reported outcome questionnaires) to therapists alone, to both therapists and patients, versus no feedback in psychotherapy. It evaluates treatment outcomes.

This RCT evaluates the routine use of standardised outcome measures (monthly postal questionnaires) with feedback versus treatment as usual in adult mental health services. The feedback (whether to clinicians or patients) is based on PROMs.

This RCT investigates the addition of personalised feedback on physical and psychological status (based on repeated patient-reported measures) to a guided self-help programme for bulimia nervosa. It compares the same programme with and without such PROMs feedback.

Despite being an RCT, this study examines the effect of patients using a symptom monitor for systematic self-reporting; the abstract does not indicate that the symptom data were fed back to healthcare providers. Without a feedback component, it does not test PROMs feedback.

This landmark RCT compares systematic symptom monitoring using electronic patient-reported outcomes (ePROs) with clinician feedback (printouts, email alerts) versus usual care. It clearly meets the inclusion criteria as a trial of PROMs feedback.

This RCT evaluates the effect of outcome monitoring feedback (based on patient-reported outcome measures) to therapists versus no feedback, and examines therapist-level moderators. It is a direct comparison of PROMs feedback.

This RCT evaluates a decision aid (video versus standard educational materials) to promote informed lung cancer screening decisions, not the provision of PROMs feedback. It does not meet the inclusion criteria.

This RCT assesses a multi-component intervention including screening, nursing assessment, and referral. Although it discloses screening results, the intervention is not limited to PROMs feedback and includes bundled components; the comparison is not solely PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

This pilot RCT compares standard toxicity monitoring plus an electronic PRO-tool (PRO-CTCAE) for adverse event reporting versus standard monitoring alone. The PRO-tool likely provides feedback to clinicians; the trial directly tests the addition of PROMs-based monitoring.

This pilot RCT evaluates an electronic symptom monitoring intervention where patient-reported symptoms are graphically presented to the clinical team during rounds, compared to usual care. It meets criteria for PROMs feedback.

This noninferiority RCT compares smartphone-based symptom and faecal calprotectin monitoring (with clinician feedback) versus standard face-to-face care. Routine patient-reported symptom feedback is a core component of the intervention, making it a trial of PROMs feedback.

This RCT evaluates an interactive e-health platform for patient self-assessment and self-monitoring. The platform provides feedback to patients about their own status, which constitutes PROMs feedback to patients. The trial compares this feedback to usual care.

This three-arm RCT tests an ecological momentary intervention involving mobile assessments with text-message feedback to reduce alcohol use. The assessments (PROMs) are combined with immediate feedback to participants, compared to assessment-only and no-contact groups.

This cluster-randomised trial evaluates continuous feedback of standardised outcome measures (weekly computerised assessments) to patients and clinicians in inpatient psychiatric care versus no feedback.

This RCT (within a larger trial) evaluates the effect of providing HAM-D scores (a depression-specific patient-reported outcome) and treatment algorithms to primary care physicians, compared to not providing such information, on treatment decision making.

This feasibility RCT compares two versions of a web-based symptom monitoring app (with reminders versus without reminders), but both arms receive the app and its feedback features. There is no control group without PROMs feedback, so it does not test the effect of feedback vs no feedback.

This pilot study evaluates an automated IVR symptom monitoring and alert intervention, but the abstract does not clearly state that patients were randomly allocated. Without evidence of randomisation, it does not meet the inclusion criteria for a randomised trial.
This article reports the development and psychometric validation of the ADDQoL questionnaire; it is not a randomised trial.

This cluster-RCT compares two strategies of feedback (generic and patient-specific) of end-of-life care quality measures (PROMs) to nursing home staff versus no feedback, assessing end-of-life outcomes. It directly tests PROMs feedback.
This is a descriptive progress report on the development of the PROMIS item banks; it is not a randomised trial.

This RCT compares nurse-led telephone follow-up with hospital follow-up in endometrial cancer; it does not involve PROMs feedback as an intervention. The study focuses on mode of follow-up, not on routine provision of PROMs feedback.

RCT: physicians received patient-specific treatment recommendations based on depression screening (PROMs feedback). Control: no intervention. Measures process of care and outcomes. Matches review criteria.

RCT: intervention group received the ITPA summary (PROMs) for clinicians; control group did not. Assesses symptom distress and care processes. Directly tests PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.
RCT comparing ESM self-monitoring with weekly feedback (PROMs feedback to patients) vs self-monitoring without feedback vs TAU. Tests effect of feedback on empowerment. Relevant to review.
RCT comparing two rehabilitation methods (Nintendo Wii vs conventional physiotherapy). Not a study of PROMs feedback to clinicians or patients.

RCT: clients in feedback condition received progress and alliance feedback (PROMs) provided to both clients and therapists. Control: TAU. Assesses outcomes and dropouts. Clearly meets inclusion criteria.
Not a randomised trial; describes development and validation of COOP Charts. No PROMs feedback intervention comparison.
RCT: patients randomised to receive PROMIS Pain Interference CAT feedback prior to surgical consultation or not. Evaluates satisfaction and communication. PROMs feedback to patients.
RCT of providing client progress feedback plus clinical support tools to therapists. Control: TAU. Tests PROMs feedback to therapists.
Systematic review, not a primary randomised trial.
RCT: practices received feedback of patient-reported asthma morbidity and treatment information. Control: no feedback. Assesses symptoms and drug use. PROMs feedback to primary care teams.
Commentary/policy analysis, not a randomised trial.
RCT: psychiatric diagnostic interview (patient-reported) results either provided to physician or not. Measures diagnosis and referral. PROMs feedback to clinicians.

Describes an experimental design with random assignment; half of physicians received patient-completed SIP (PROM) report prior to visit. Measures awareness and communication. Likely an RCT of PROMs feedback.
Controlled study but not clearly randomised; allocation not described as random. Ineligible design.
RCT comparing two active mHealth interventions, both involving PROMs feedback to clinicians; no true 'no feedback' control group. Does not isolate effect of PROMs feedback vs none.
RCT of a surgical/procedural intervention (stellate ganglion block) for PTSD; not related to PROMs feedback.
Feasibility RCT: patients monitored with PROMs (PHQ, etc.), feedback of scores to patients at practitioners' discretion. Control: usual care. Tests PROMs feedback in depression.
RCT: clinicians received SCL-90-based feedback reports vs no reports. Assesses mental health outcomes. PROMs feedback to clinicians.
Cluster RCT: DIALOG intervention provided immediate feedback of patient-reported QoL and needs ratings during consultations. Control: TAU. Tests structured PROMs feedback and discussion.
Abstract describes a study on HRQoL changes during a weight management programme; no randomisation to PROMs feedback vs no feedback. Not an RCT of feedback.
RCT: feedback of GHQ screening results to primary care clinicians vs no feedback. Assesses detection and management. PROMs feedback to clinicians.
RCT: therapists and patients received progress feedback and decision-support tools. Control: TAU. Tests PROMs feedback to therapists and patients.
RCT: GPs used a self-rating depression scale (MADRS) in recurrent consultations with feedback discussion. Control: TAU. Tests PROMs feedback in primary care depression management.
Systematic review, not a primary randomised trial.

RCT: physical function assessments (performance tests and self-report) with feedback to participants and their physicians, or assessment alone. Control: no feedback? Evaluates functional decline and health status. PROMs feedback to patients and physicians.
Review/guideline paper, not a randomised trial.
Qualitative study, not a randomised trial.
Study protocol for an RCT of web-based CBT; not a study of PROMs feedback. Also, not a completed trial.
Bibliographic study, not a randomised trial.

RCT: children completed the eSAID questionnaire (PROM) and gave the report to their dentist; control completed only two items. Assesses anxiety, satisfaction, cooperation. PROMs feedback to clinicians and patients.

RCT: diabetes nurse assessed and discussed psychological well-being (PROM) with patients in addition to standard care. Control: standard care. Tests PROMs feedback and discussion on mood and satisfaction.
Commentary/perspective article, not a randomised trial.
Not a randomised trial comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback. It tested different components of tailored messages, all groups received feedback. No clinical practice setting.
Qualitative study, not a randomised trial.
Randomised trial comparing PHQ-9 screening/feedback to providers vs no feedback on depressive symptoms.
Validation study of a hearing screening questionnaire, not a randomised trial comparing feedback.
Feedback of physiological (heart rate) data, not patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). Not a clinical practice study.
Cluster randomised trial implementing discharge readiness assessment (PROM) with feedback to nurses/patients vs usual care.
Both groups received clinician summaries of PROMs; intervention added self-care components, not feedback vs no feedback.
No mention of randomisation; likely a non-randomised study on screening feedback.
Randomised trial providing OQ-45 feedback to therapists vs no feedback for patients at risk in psychosomatic inpatient therapy.
Literature review, not a primary trial.
Syndromic surveillance system evaluation, not a randomised trial of PROMs feedback in clinical practice.
Randomised trial of HRQoL measurement with feedback to clinicians vs no feedback in lung transplant follow-up.
Randomised trial of a web-based asthma self-management system including PROMs self-monitoring and feedback vs usual care (conservative inclusion).
Randomised trial comparing minimal distress screening (likely no feedback) vs full screening with personalized report feedback in cancer outpatients.
Discussion/debate article, not a trial.
Communication skills training for oncologists, not PROMs feedback intervention.
Randomised trial of case-finding: GDS scores fed back to physicians vs no feedback in elderly primary care.
Controlled study with random disclosure of BDI scores to GPs vs non-disclosure; essentially a randomised comparison of feedback.
Communication-priming intervention to increase goals-of-care discussions, not PROMs feedback.
Commentary/opinion piece, not a trial.
Study design and recruitment description; no outcome data.
Tailored cancer risk information based on patient data, not specifically PROMs feedback.
Randomised trial of telephone follow-up after surgery; not an intervention of PROMs feedback.
Systematic review, not a primary trial.
Guideline methodology paper, not a trial.
Conceptual paper on comorbidity, not a trial.
Randomised trial of web-based symptom self-reporting with nurse practitioner review/feedback vs standard care in breast cancer.
Secondary analysis of an RCT (FOCUS) examining effect modification by IQ; not a primary trial comparing feedback vs no feedback.
Randomised trial of HRQoL measurement with feedback to physicians vs no feedback in chronic liver disease.
Overview of phase III trials, not a primary study.
Implementation strategy trial to improve guideline adherence; not specifically testing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.
Description of reference management software; not a study.
